# Writing Sample 02 — "Eagle of Alamut" Ch. 2 (human-written, craft reference only)

> Source: teecup_angel, *Eagle of Alamut* (Assassin's Creed), AO3 work 44196343.
> Style reference only. Study the craft; never copy words, names, characters, or plot.

## What to notice here

- A long stretch of the chapter is just Desmond thinking on a rooftop, and it stays gripping
  because the internal voice is restless and human. Note how planning is rendered: not a tidy
  bulleted risk assessment, but a person talking themselves in circles, getting a headache,
  swearing at time travel, landing on a decision.
- Canon knowledge (the year 1181, Solomon's Temple, the Apple, Masyaf, Alamut) is used as the
  character's own reasoning, never as exposition dumped for the reader.
- The quiet domestic scene (the borrowed clothes, the herb tea, "Do you wish to talk about it?"
  "No.") carries more weight than any action beat. Emotion first.
- Zero em dashes. Contrast-for-emphasis is almost never used; statements are positive and plain.

## Excerpt

The woman's home was just a simple three-minute walk through the main street but that was all Desmond needed to know to be certain of where he was.

Jerusalem.

To be more exact, the poor part of Jerusalem.

...

"With what money?" the woman asked as she used a wooden ladle to steer the pot.

"Uh…" Desmond rubbed the back of his neck as he said in an almost questioning tone, "I'll find work somewhere in the city?"

The woman chuckled as she shook her head. "I'm sure you'll find something in the city tomorrow."

Desmond's lips curved into a grim smile as he asked, "You're… not worried?"

"That you might rob me while I sleep?" She didn't even wait for him to reply. "You're free to try and find anything that you might be able to sell but I'm afraid you'll find nothing. Whatever valuable I had has long been taken or sold."

...

"Do you wish to talk about it?" she asked gently as she took a sip of her own cup.

Desmond knew that his expression was giving him away but, at the same time, he didn't want to try and force a mask on himself right now.

However…

"No," he said softly before taking another sip.

"That's fine," the woman said, her expression filled with understanding.

With those words, Desmond relaxed. As the night passed by in comfortable silence and gentle warmth.

...

A few hours later, Desmond finally took the time to relax on top of one of the rooftops of the church in the Middle District, relaxing his back against the cross behind him.

He had no idea what the church's name was. Abstergo's Animus didn't have a Shaun to add historical information to any landmark.

Which was annoying, because this meant that Desmond had no idea what was supposed to happen.

On his way to finding clothes that actually fit him, he found papers from the Rich District (hey, if he was going to steal, he was going to steal from the rich) that indicated the year was 1181.

Which meant Altaïr was 16 years old right now. Just like Desmond's body.

And that… Was a problem.

...

Okay then. New plan. Ignore the time travel bullshit of this entire thing.

The only way to make sure the world would be saved in 2012 was to make sure that history played as it should.

...

Sometimes, Desmond found himself thinking that he was the world's personal chew toy.

That was the only reason he could think of for why his 'carefully thought out' plan would go down the drain so quickly.

...

Desmond's eyes widened. Alamut. He could go to Alamut.

He could become an Alamut Assassin, keep an eye on Masyaf and Altaïr through the grapevine, then join the squad that gives monthly reports during the time the Apple would be in Masyaf.

Yes. That could work.

Desmond took a deep breath and looked at the sky. The sun was only starting to rise.

He had time to prepare. And… to say goodbye.
